nodes.name: Slack Trigger - New Ticket Message
nodes.notes: 6.3.1.1. FLAG: SLACK_SUPPORT_CHANNEL_ID is a new env var, not in the existing §10A.2 consolidated list - add it once a real support Slack channel exists. Also flag per §0.3: Slack->Linear here is an internal issue-tracking wiring, distinct from the still-undecided customer-facing helpdesk tool (Chatwoot) - these may need to be reconciled into one system later; not done automatically here since that's a tool-stack decision for Nivy, not something to assume.

nodes.name: Filter Root Messages Only
nodes.notes: PLACEHOLDER heuristic (root message, non-bot, >5 chars = candidate ticket) - no rule for 'what counts as a new ticket' exists in the uploads. Flag for Nivy to confirm or replace (e.g. require a specific emoji reaction, a slash command, or a dedicated intake channel instead of free-text detection).

parameters.query:
-- try to resolve which client this Slack user/channel maps to, so the ticket count increments the right row.
-- FLAG: no existing mapping table between Slack users and clients_master exists in this stack today -
-- this SELECT will very likely return 0 rows until such a mapping is built. Ticket is still created in
-- Linear either way; only the internal support_ticket_count increment depends on a match.
SELECT id AS client_id FROM clients_master WHERE email = {{ JSON.stringify($json.slack_user) }} LIMIT 1;

nodes.name: Attempt Client Match
nodes.notes: REQUIRES SCHEMA CONFIRMATION / real mapping - this lookup is a best-effort placeholder (matching Slack user id against clients_master.email, which will not actually match in practice). Flagging rather than pretending this resolves reliably.

nodes.name: Linear Ticket-Create
nodes.notes: 6.3.1.2. Linear's GraphQL API (issueCreate mutation) - standard integration pattern for Linear, no invented endpoint. LINEAR_API_KEY and LINEAR_SUPPORT_TEAM_ID are new env vars, not yet in §10A.2's list - add once a real Linear workspace/team is confirmed.

value.payload: ={{ { linear_issue_id: $json.data?.issueCreate?.issue?.id, linear_issue_url: $json.data?.issueCreate?.issue?.url, message_text: $('Filter Root Messages Only').item.json.message_text } }}

nodes.name: Report to Hub
nodes.notes: S6.4 — the Slack trigger itself is an external entry point (same category as Cal.com/Typebot/Documenso per the plan's own rollout notes) and correctly stays as-is, no independent-polling to remove here. What was missing was the *outbound* hand-off: this gives event_type: support.ticket_logged (named in the plan's S6.2 text but previously had no producer) a real source. Fires regardless of whether the Slack-user-to-client match succeeds, since the ticket is created either way — client_id is null on an unmatched ticket, same as the existing Log Unmatched Ticket branch. Not yet wired into Hub-Dispatcher (no consumer subscribes yet per S0-EVENT-TYPE-TAXONOMY.md).

nodes.name: Increment support_ticket_count
nodes.notes: 6.3.1.3. Column added via ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS per the master plan's own data-model rule (§0.4.7).

subSteps.6.3.1.1: Slack trigger node (new ticket message) -> Slack Trigger + Filter Root Messages Only (placeholder ticket-detection heuristic) + Is New Ticket?
subSteps.6.3.1.2: Linear ticket-create node -> Linear Ticket-Create (GraphQL issueCreate)
subSteps.6.3.1.3: Postgres update - support_ticket_count increment -> Attempt Client Match + Client Matched? + Increment support_ticket_count / Log Unmatched Ticket
subSteps.S6.4: Report to Hub node -> event_type: support.ticket_logged, added per star-topology plan. Slack Trigger stays as an external entry point (not a polling loop, so nothing removed there) — the fix is giving this module's outbound hand-off a Hub report, same pattern as other event-triggered spokes.
